clue.text: Ambitious professionals air secrets freely

indicators.note: letters arranged freely are let loose from their order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pushy executives are leaking confidential information without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone set on climbing the ladder at any cost is a careerist, an ambitious professional by definition.

clue.text: A carer said to be one who listens

indicators.note: said to be points to how a phrase sounds when spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: a carer is a tender, someone who tends, so the phrase gives 'a tender'

explanation.surface: A care worker is described as someone good at hearing people out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tender' (a carer) spoken aloud runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An attender is one who pays attention, heeding or listening to what is said.

clue.text: Cat, one in the doctor's surgery?

definitions.meaning: a cat kept to catch rodents
MO is a medical officer, a doctor, and a user of the surgery is a patient there

explanation.surface: A feline spotted sitting in the GP's waiting room.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: MO (medical officer) plus USER, someone making use of the doctor's practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat valued for catching vermin, the common sense of the word.

clue.text: Firm concerned with making money

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to be in something is to be involved or concerned with it

explanation.surface: A business whose sole interest is profit-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins are metal currency, so the word stands for money in general.

clue.text: Friend's travelling north, needing public transport schedules

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ally is a friend; with the 's it gives ALLYS
buses are public transport

explanation.surface: A pal heads up north and has to check bus timetables.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'north' is upwards, so 'travelling north' signals the friend's letters reading from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabuses are outlines or programmes of study, a sense close to schedules of work.

clue.text: Capital city worker, one in the past undermining society

indicators.note: in a down clue, to undermine something is to sit beneath it, so these pieces come below the abbreviation for society

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker
I is the Roman numeral one
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A labourer in the capital once worked to subvert the social order.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital of Chile.

clue.text: Viewers' angles taken on board by American thinkers

indicators.note: what is taken on board is carried inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Points of view absorbed by US philosophers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewers' are eyes: the canthi are the corners where the eyelids meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The canthi are the corners of the eye, so they are the angles of an organ that views.

clue.text: Goddess is number one female

parts.note: I as the first person, oneself, is number one
a sis, short for sister, is a female relative

explanation.surface: A goddess holds top place among women.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the chief goddess of ancient Egypt, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: Lots of stories? Maybe Burgess keeps record, releasing any number

indicators.note: a word that keeps something holds it within
releasing means letting go, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Anthony Burgess, author of A Clockwork Orange; Maybe says Burgess is one example of the name
N is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A writer holding on to a document, letting a figure go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' warns that Burgess stands for his first name, as other Anthonys would; 'releasing' drops the N, and 'keeps' holds the record inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthology is a published collection, often of short stories or poems.

clue.text: A mother's one who wrote animal tales

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother; with the 's it gives DAMS

explanation.surface: A mum is someone who penned stories about creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Adams wrote Watership Down, a novel about rabbits.

clue.text: American author being without power to engage me

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, as gears mesh, so these letters go inside
without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a being is a person
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A writer powerless to draw me in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the power symbol, and 'to engage' sets me inside the rest just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century US essayist and poet.

clue.text: Little child in stories making understatement

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, signalled by in

parts.note: stories are lies, fibs
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster in fairy tales is said to play things down.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that affirms by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad', a form of understatement.

clue.text: Haggard writer who is on a journey?

definitions.meaning: The writer is named by his middle name
one travelling on horseback or by bus or bike

explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like an adjective meaning gaunt; it is the novelist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider is the name H. Rider Haggard wrote under, and it also means a traveller on a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Two groups of stars putting out ace literary collections

indicators.note: putting out means expelling, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Libra and Aries are two constellations, groups of stars
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: Two constellations lose a star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two adjacent As in LIBRA ARIES goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Libraries are collections of books, so of literary works.

clue.text: Males arise to be trained for Buddhist institutions

indicators.note: what is trained is reshaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men get up to be schooled in monasteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamaseries are monasteries of Tibetan Buddhist lamas.

clue.text: Shaky alarms repaired without a high-level security officer

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged
without means leaving out, so the letter a is taken from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Faulty alarms being fixed without a senior guard.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAKY ALARMS minus one A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky marshal is an armed guard on an aircraft, high-level in the sense of airborne.

clue.text: Mother's boy is lad turning into an Oxford man of books

indicators.note: turning about changes order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mummy's boy grows up to become an Oxford bookman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Bodley founded Oxford's Bodleian Library in 1602.

clue.text: Difficulty of driver initially getting into gear

indicators.note: getting into means going inside, so a letter is placed within

parts.note: a harness is gear, equipment or tackle

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A motorist struggles to change gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardness is the quality of being hard, i.e. difficulty.

clue.text: Keeps going, getting to peak as the final destination

parts.note: something that lasts keeps going
a top is a peak

explanation.surface: Persevering to reach the summit as the ultimate goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The last stop is the terminus of a route, the final destination.

clue.text: Authors rested with girl, having crossed street

parts.note: sat means rested

indicators.note: the girl has crossed the street, so she straddles it and its letters go inside

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Writers took a break with a girl after crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Satirists are writers of satire, so authors of a kind.

clue.text: Loveless Germanic god has everyone in bondage

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, O, and loveless means that letter is removed

parts.note: Thor is the Norse and Germanic god of thunder
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A god without love keeps everyone enslaved.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrall is servitude, the state of being in bondage.

clue.text: Book from those academics

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A volume issued by certain scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is a book of the Old Testament, named for a prophet.

clue.text: Endless inferno encountered in protective headgear

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: an inferno is hell
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A never-ending blaze met by someone wearing a hard hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is a hard hat worn to guard the head.

clue.text: American author presents fat emperor coming to premature end

parts.note: lard is fat

indicators.note: a premature end cuts the word short, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A writer serves up an overweight ruler dying young.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring Lardner was a US sportswriter and short-story writer.

clue.text: Grass as a rule needing nitrogen

parts.note: a law is a rule
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Turf generally needs nitrogen fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' reads like 'usually'; only 'a rule' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is an area of mown grass.

clue.text: Books taking a time to get fantastic sales

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Volumes take a while to sell spectacularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlases are books of maps.

clue.text: Not much attire, going topless

indicators.note: topless means without its top, which in a down clue is the first letter

parts.note: a habit is attire, as a nun's dress

explanation.surface: Skimpy clothing worn without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit is a small amount, so not much.

clue.text: SF author in small city

definitions.meaning: H. G. ... wrote science fiction such as The Time Machine
the cathedral city in Somerset, England's smallest city

explanation.definitionFit: Wells is both the surname of the science-fiction writer H. G. Wells and the tiny cathedral city in Somerset, England.

clue.text: French author turning green, zeal destroyed — nothing penned

indicators.note: turning round reverses the order of letters

parts.note: lime is a shade of green

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so a letter is enclosed
something destroyed is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A French writer goes green, zeal wrecked, with nothing written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the citrus green; 'destroyed' rearranges zeal to EZLA, and 'penned' encloses the zero for EZOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola was the French naturalist novelist who wrote Germinal and J'accuse.
